title: Averaging Weights Leads to Wider Optima and Better Generalization
venue: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
publication_status_observed: Proceedings of the 34th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence (UAI); arXiv preprint arXiv:1803.05407v3
main_claims: Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA) — averaging SGD iterates with cyclical or constant learning rates — finds much wider optima than SGD and consistently improves generalization.

SGD with cyclical/constant learning rates traverses the periphery of a set of high-performing weight solutions; SWA moves toward the center of this set, yielding flatter and better-generalizing solutions.
SWA approximates Fast Geometric Ensembling (FGE) with a single model at essentially no additional computational overhead.
methodology: SWA averages model weights collected at minimum learning rate points (cyclical schedule) or at each epoch (constant schedule) after initial SGD training. Evaluated on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 (VGG-16, Preactivation ResNet-164, WRN-28-10, Shake-Shake, PyramidNet-272) and ImageNet (ResNet-50/152, DenseNet-161). Flatness/width of optima compared via loss landscape visualization along random directions and the SWA-SGD line segment.
key_results: SWA improves WRN-28-10 accuracy on CIFAR-100 from 80.82% (SGD) to 81.46%–82.15% (1–1.5 budgets).
SWA improves ResNet-50 on ImageNet from 76.15% to 76.97% (top-1) with 10 epochs of averaging.
SWA finds solutions in flatter loss basins than SGD: much further displacement is needed to increase test error by a given amount from SWA compared to SGD.
limitations: SWA uses a single final average rather than an ensemble, which limits the diversity of predictions compared to FGE.
SWA finds solutions in the same loss basin as SGD initialization; it does not escape to different basins.
The paper does not evaluate OOD generalization on corruption benchmarks; improvements are shown on standard i.i.d. test sets.
relevance_to_rq: Directly relevant to the weight_averaging and flat_minima_for_dg sub-topics: SWA is the flat-minima-oriented control optimizer in the RQ's experiment. The paper establishes that SWA finds flatter solutions than SGD by a different mechanism (weight trajectory averaging) than SAM (adversarial perturbation), motivating using SWA as a control to separate flatness from optimization trajectory effects.

key_quotes.text: SWA procedure finds much flatter solutions than SGD, and approximates the recent Fast Geometric Ensembling (FGE) approach with a single model.
key_quotes.context: Main claim about SWA finding flat minima

key_quotes.text: SGD generally converges to a point near the boundary of the wide flat region of optimal points. SWA on the other hand is able to find a point centered in this region
key_quotes.context: Geometric intuition explaining why SWA finds flatter solutions than SGD

key_quotes.text: SWA is not finding a different minima than SGD, but rather a flatter region in the same basin of attraction.
key_quotes.context: Clarification of SWA's relationship to SGD's basin of attraction
